question: Bind — ATK, 8-7, you are UP 3v2 and carry the spike with an Operator scoped down A Short. One defender was just traded on A. How do you play the spike-carrier-with-Op?

options.label: Hold the Op locked on A Short, let your two teammates take the space, and plant only once it's safe
options.explication_courte: Up 3v2 as the spike carrier, you must be the last to die and the Op is a hold weapon. Locking A Short punishes any defender re-peek from the choke while your mates clear the site, then you plant safe — numbers advantage preserved.

sources_option.citation: The Op holds an angle the enemy must cross; the spike carrier plays last and safe to convert a numbers lead into a plant

options.label: Wide-swing A Short with the Op to hunt the last two defenders yourself
options.explication_courte: Swinging the Op forfeits its holding advantage and exposes the spike carrier to a trade — losing that duel drops your 3v2 to a 2v2 with the objective forward and no cover.

sources_option.citation: Wide-swinging with an Operator surrenders its holding advantage; doing it as the carrier risks the objective

options.label: Plant immediately where you stand to bank the plant before contesting anything
options.explication_courte: Getting the plant down is valuable, but planting too early in an exposed spot without your Op holding the choke can let the two defenders re-peek and contest the plant. Usually you secure the angle first, then plant.

sources_option.citation: A plant secures round equity, but planting exposed before the entries are controlled invites a contested defuse fight

options.label: Leave A entirely and rotate the spike toward B for a re-fake
options.explication_courte: Abandoning a won 3v2 on A to walk the spike across the map wastes your advantage and the clock, and risks running the objective into an unknown rotation. When you're up on-site, you close it out, not re-fake.

sources_option.citation: Walking the objective away from a won site position surrenders tempo and the numbers advantage you already earned

explication_longue: This is a carrier-and-Op discipline decision with a numbers lead. Up 8-7 in a 3v2 on Bind, you hold an Operator scoped down A Short and carry the spike after your team traded a defender on A. The optimal line stacks two rules that agree: the spike carrier must be the last to die, and the Op is a weapon you hold with. Locking A Short punishes any defender who re-peeks the choke while your two teammates take the space, and then you plant only once it is safe — your 3v2 stays intact and the round is nearly closed. Wide-swinging the Op to hunt the last two yourself is the costly error: you forfeit the Op's holding edge and expose the carrier to a trade that would drop you to a 2v2 with the objective forward. Planting immediately where you stand is genuinely acceptable — banking the plant has value — but doing it exposed, before your Op has locked the choke, invites the two defenders to re-peek and contest the defuse; usually you secure the angle first. Leaving A to re-fake toward B is the faute: it throws away a won 3v2 and the clock, and risks running the spike into an unknown rotation. Hold the choke, let your mates clear, plant safe.

sources.citation: Spike carrier with an Op: hold the choke the enemy must cross, play last and safe, and plant once the site is controlled
